title: Two Prisoners Executed in Ghezel Hesar Prison in Karaj
content:
According to HRANA, two prisoners were executed in Ghezel Hesar Prison.

HRANA has confirmed the identities of the prisoners as Amrollah Seiri, a resident of Varamin, and Shokri (first name unknown), a resident of Markazi Province. Both prisoners were hanged at dawn today, Wednesday, October 28, 2026.

According to information obtained by HRANA, the two prisoners had previously been arrested on murder charges in separate cases and were subsequently sentenced to death by criminal courts.

As of the time of this report, the executions have not been officially announced by prison authorities or other relevant institutions.

Between October 10, 2025, and October 8, 2026, HRANA documented at least 2,003 executions across Iran, based on 1,857 reports, representing an increase of approximately 29% compared to the previous reporting period. During the same period, HRANA also documented 230 death sentences. For more detailed statistics and analysis of executions in Iran, read HRANA’s latest comprehensive report.
snippet: According to HRANA, two prisoners were executed in Ghezel Hesar Prison.
sourceDescription: Human Rights Activists News Agency Hrana – News Agency | Human Rights Activists News Agency

title: Artin Ghazanfari, Baha’i Citizen, Sentenced to 26 Years in Prison
content:
Under a verdict issued by Branch 15 of the Tehran Revolutionary Court, presided over by Judge Abolghasem Salavati, and communicated to him on Monday, Artin Ghazanfari was sentenced to a total of 26 years in prison.

An informed source close to Ghazanfari’s family told HRANA: “Mr. Ghazanfari was sentenced to 20 years in prison on the charge of ‘media-related activities,’ five years for ‘assembly and collusion against national security,’ and one year for ‘propaganda against the regime.’ Although the punishment for the first charge was stated to be 10 years in prison, the judge imposed a 20-year sentence by invoking the Law on Intensifying Punishment for Espionage.”

According to information obtained by HRANA, Ghazanfari’s physical condition has been reported as poor due to several medical conditions, including heart failure, asthma, and high blood pressure. Despite prison medical staff emphasizing the necessity of transferring him to medical facilities outside the prison, he continues to be denied access to specialized medical treatment outside the prison due to opposition from the judge overseeing his case.

title: Teacher Union Activist Mahnaz Ebrahimi Arrested in Shiraz
content:
According to HRANA, on the morning of Tuesday, October 27, 2026, Mahnaz Ebrahimi, a mathematics teacher and a teachers’ union activist, was arrested by security forces.

The Fars Teachers’ Trade Association, which reported the arrest, stated that security forces entered Ebrahimi’s home, arrested her, and subsequently transferred her to Adelabad Prison in Shiraz.

As of the time of this report, no information has been released regarding the reasons for her arrest, the charges against her, or the status of her legal case.
snippet: According to HRANA, on the morning of Tuesday, October 27, 2026, Mahnaz Ebrahimi, a mathematics teacher and a teachers’ union activist, was arrested by security forces.
sourceDescription: Human Rights Activists News Agency Hrana – News Agency | Human Rights Activists News Agency

title: Two Prisoners Executed in Shahr-e Kord and Kashan Prisons
content:
According to HRANA, citing Iran Human Rights Organization, Ali Mokhtari, 30, was executed on the morning of Sunday, October 25, 2026, in Shahr-e Kord Prison.

Mokhtari had been sentenced to death on charges of “rape.” According to the report, he was unmarried and had been in detention for approximately two years. An informed source stated that he had been accused of raping a married woman, an allegation he consistently denied.

In a separate report, Iran Human Rights Organization announced the execution of another prisoner, identified as Davood Rokhbin, 40, a married father of one from Kashan.

According to the report, Rokhbin was executed yesterday, October 27, in Kashan Prison.

He had been arrested five years earlier on murder charges following a group altercation and was subsequently sentenced to death by judicial authorities.

As of the time of this report, neither execution has been officially announced by prison authorities or other relevant institutions.
snippet: According to HRANA, citing Iran Human Rights Organization, Ali Mokhtari, 30, was executed on the morning of Sunday, October 25, 2026, in Shahr-e Kord Prison.
sourceDescription: Human Rights Activists News Agency Hrana – News Agency | Human Rights Activists News Agency

title: Film Director Jafar Panahi Sentenced to Prison, Asset Confiscation, and Additional Penalties
content:
According to HRANA, citing Emtedad, Mostafa Nili, Jafar Panahi’s lawyer, has announced that his client has been sentenced to imprisonment and additional penalties in a new case.

Nili stated that Branch 26 of the Tehran Revolutionary Court sentenced his client to five years and one month of discretionary imprisonment and ordered the confiscation of all his movable and immovable assets. Under the ruling, Panahi was also sentenced to a two-year ban on social media activity and a two-year prohibition on leaving the country.

Explaining how he learned of the new case, the lawyer said that last week, after his client’s bank accounts were frozen, he visited the Sentence Enforcement Office of the Culture and Media Prosecutor’s Office, where he discovered that the verdict had been issued in absentia. According to Nili, the case file stated that Panahi was outside Iran, although he had returned to the country on March 30, 2026, during the 40-day war.
snippet: According to HRANA, citing Emtedad, Mostafa Nili, Jafar Panahi’s lawyer, has announced that his client has been sentenced to imprisonment and additional penalties in a new case.
sourceDescription: Human Rights Activists News Agency Hrana – News Agency | Human Rights Activists News Agency

title: Lithuania Reports Arrest of Two of Its Citizens in Iran
content:
On Tuesday, October 27, 2026, Lithuania’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs announced that it had received official information from Iranian authorities confirming the detention of two Lithuanian nationals. Responding to media inquiries, the ministry emphasized that, out of respect for the individuals’ privacy and without their consent, it could not disclose their identities or provide information about the circumstances and details of their arrests.

The announcement comes after Lithuanian police previously reported that two Lithuanian women, Daiva Zakažauskaitė and Erika Šlimaitė, had gone missing while traveling in Iran. However, Lithuania’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs has not identified the detained citizens by name.

The Lithuanian Foreign Ministry also stated: “We continue to make every effort to ensure that the detained individuals receive the necessary consular assistance.”

So far, no information has been released regarding the reasons for their arrests, any potential charges against them, or their place of detention.
snippet: On Tuesday, October 27, 2026, Lithuania’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs announced that it had received official information from Iranian authorities confirming the detention of two Lithuanian nationals.
sourceDescription: Human Rights Activists News Agency Hrana – News Agency | Human Rights Activists News Agency

title: Azerbaijani-Turk Activist Naser Razmjou Arrested in Ardabil
content:
According to HRANA, the news agency of Human Rights Activists in Iran, Naser Razmjou has been arrested.

Based on information received by HRANA, Razmjou was arrested this morning at his residence in Ardabil. Following his arrest, he was transferred to an undisclosed location.

Previously, on Saturday, May 16, 2026, Razmjou, along with 12 other citizens in a joint case, was sentenced by the East Azerbaijan Province Court of Appeals to two years and nine months in prison on suspicion of membership in an illegal group and an additional three years and seven months on charges of “assembly and collusion against national security.”

Earlier, in late December 2025, these individuals had been sentenced to a combined total of 85 years and nine months in prison by Branch 2 of the Tabriz Revolutionary Court in the initial proceedings.

Razmjou had also previously been arrested by security forces on October 21, 2023. He was subsequently released from Tabriz Prison on November 30 of that year after posting bail of 500 million tomans.

At the time of this report, no information has been obtained regarding the reasons for the Azerbaijani-Turk activist’s latest arrest or his place of detention.
snippet: According to HRANA, the news agency of Human Rights Activists in Iran, Naser Razmjou has been arrested.
sourceDescription: Human Rights Activists News Agency Hrana – News Agency | Human Rights Activists News Agency

title: Hojjat Moghaddam Arrested by Security Forces in Birjand
content:
Based on information received by HRANA, Hojjat (Yaser) Moghaddam was arrested by Ministry of Intelligence agents on Sunday, October 25, while traveling along a street. He faces charges of “propaganda against the regime” and “spreading false information to disturb public opinion.”

An informed source close to his family confirmed the arrest to HRANA, stating: “On the morning of Monday, October 26, security authorities contacted Moghaddam’s family and informed them of the charges against him and the agency responsible for his arrest. He had previously been sentenced to imprisonment but has not yet received a summons to begin serving his sentence.”

Hojjat (Yaser) Moghaddam faces two separate sets of legal proceedings. In the first part of his case, he faces charges including “resisting officers in the performance of their duties” and “disrupting public order and peace.” His case remains under review at Branch 102 of the Criminal Court Two of Birjand. A hearing on these charges was held on August 15, 2025.

title: Karun: Detention Orders Extended for 12 Citizens in the “Qaleh Chanaan” Case
content:
According to HRANA, the detention orders of 12 citizens involved in the “Qaleh Chanaan” case have been extended.

According to information received by HRANA, alongside the extension of their detention orders, a hearing in their case, originally scheduled for October 23, has been postponed for one month.

The 12 individuals, Tofigh Silavi, Mohammad Neisi, Hossein Silavi, Hamed Zohairi, Taregh Hosnian, Bahador Zargani, Mansour Naseri, Ahmad Bavi-Fard, Yousef Hosnian, Jassem Bavi, Mohammad Ali Bavi, and Hamid Hosnian, attended an interrogation session on October 12, 2026, at Branch 2 of the Karun Prosecutor’s Office, presided over by Judge Vadi-Nejad. The session was previously reported by HRANA.

During the session, the individuals faced charges including “disrupting public order and peace,” “moharebeh (enmity against God) through shooting at Basij bases,” “baghi (armed rebellion) through an armed uprising against the establishment,” and “assembly and collusion against national security.” The charges of moharebeh and baghi, both of which can carry the death penalty, have heightened families’ concerns about the possibility of death sentences being issued.
snippet: According to HRANA, the detention orders of 12 citizens involved in the “Qaleh Chanaan” case have been extended.
sourceDescription: Human Rights Activists News Agency Hrana – News Agency | Human Rights Activists News Agency

title: Nabi Soufi Sentenced to Three Years and Six Months in Prison
content:
According to HRANA, citing Kolbarnews, Nabi Soufi has been sentenced to prison.

According to the report, Mr. Soufi was sentenced to three years and six months of discretionary imprisonment by the Public and Revolutionary Court of Shahin Dezh.

While the report does not specify the charges on which Soufi’s prison sentence was based, it states that the legal proceedings against him stemmed from a story he posted on his Instagram account. Mr. Soufi is currently temporarily released on bail.

Nabi Soufi is married, has one child, is originally from Shahin Dezh, and resides in Tehran.
snippet: According to HRANA, citing Kolbarnews, Nabi Soufi has been sentenced to prison.
sourceDescription: Human Rights Activists News Agency Hrana – News Agency | Human Rights Activists News Agency

title: Hassan Golshan-Nejad Sentenced to Death in Connection with January 2026 Protests
content:
Based on information received by HRANA, Branch 5 of the Mashhad Revolutionary Court sentenced Hassan Golshan-Nejad to death on the charge of “carrying out operational activities in favor of Israel.” The death sentence was communicated to him today. The case against him was opened in connection with his participation in protest gatherings in January 2026.

Hassan Golshan-Nejad was arrested on February 24, 2026, while drinking coffee at a friend’s café. Following his arrest, agents took him to his home and confiscated a legally registered hunting rifle and his mobile phones.

After his arrest, Golshan-Nejad was held in solitary confinement for 10 days at The Ministry of Intelligence’s detention facility before being transferred to Ward 6/1 of Vakilabad Prison in Mashhad. He has remained in this prison ever since.

Hassan Golshan-Nejad, 36, is self-employed and the father of an eight-year-old son.
snippet: Based on information received by HRANA, Branch 5 of the Mashhad Revolutionary Court sentenced Hassan Golshan-Nejad to death on the charge of “carrying out operational activities in favor of Israel.”
sourceDescription: Human Rights Activists News Agency Hrana – News Agency | Human Rights Activists News Agency

title: Several Citizens Arrested in Hormozgan Province by IRGC Intelligence Forces
content:
According to HRANA, citing the Islamic Republic of Iran Broadcasting (IRIB), the IRGC Intelligence Organization has announced the arrest of several individuals in Hormozgan Province.

The report alleges that, during the military conflict, the detainees recorded photographs and videos of missile impact sites and military personnel positions and sent them to the Iran International television network.

Four individuals, including three women, appear in the published video of the detainees’ forced confessions.

So far, no information has been released regarding the identities of those arrested, the exact dates of their arrests, or their places of detention.
snippet: According to HRANA, citing the Islamic Republic of Iran Broadcasting (IRIB), the IRGC Intelligence Organization has announced the arrest of several individuals in Hormozgan Province.
sourceDescription: Human Rights Activists News Agency Hrana – News Agency | Human Rights Activists News Agency

title: Fars News Agency Denies Death Sentence for Melika Azizi, Reports Six-Month Prison Term
content:
According to HRANA, citing Fars News Agency, Melika Azizi has been sentenced to six months in prison.

According to the report, Ms. Azizi was arrested during the December 2025 protests in Masal County and subsequently sentenced by the judiciary to six months of discretionary imprisonment.

The media outlet, which is affiliated with security institutions, rejected reports that a death sentence had been issued against Azizi. It also claimed that she has already served two months of her sentence and will soon be released from prison after completing half of her six-month prison term.

The report did not provide further details, including the prison where she is being held or the charges brought against her.
snippet: According to HRANA, citing Fars News Agency, Melika Azizi has been sentenced to six months in prison.
sourceDescription: Human Rights Activists News Agency Hrana – News Agency | Human Rights Activists News Agency

title: Nemat Afshar Arrested in Qazvin
content:
Based on information received by HRANA, Nemat Afshar was arrested on Monday, October 26, 2026, at his residence in Qazvin by local IRGC Intelligence agents.

A source close to his family confirmed the news to HRANA, stating: “About a month ago, the relevant authorities contacted Mr. Afshar’s bail guarantor regarding his previous conviction and informed them that he was required to report to prison to serve his sentence. However, no precise information has yet been obtained regarding the reason for Nemat Afshar’s arrest or his whereabouts. This uncertainty has raised concerns among his family and relatives.”

In April 2025, the Court of Appeals upheld Mr. Afshar’s sentence of three years and six months in prison, along with a two-year travel ban and a two-year prohibition on online activities.

In November 2024, Nemat Afshar, along with three other individuals, Azam Ahooghalandar, Hossein Jafari, and Mehdi Touhidi, was sentenced by Branch 3 of the Karaj Revolutionary Court in a joint case. The four defendants received a combined total of 14 years and 10 months in prison, along with additional penalties.

Nemat Afshar is unmarried and resides in Qazvin.
snippet: Based on information received by HRANA, Nemat Afshar was arrested on Monday, October 26, 2026, at his residence in Qazvin by local IRGC Intelligence agents.
sourceDescription: Human Rights Activists News Agency Hrana – News Agency | Human Rights Activists News Agency
